title: Actualizing the Research Tasks of Military-Technical Translation/Interpreting
content: The purpose of this article is to actualize the research tasks of military-technical translation/interpreting as one of the three primary functional-pragmatic sub-types of military translation/interpreting. Despite numerous academic publications addressing the theoretical issues of military-technical translation/interpreting, its foundational conceptual provisions remain insufficiently developed and lack definitive formalization as structured theoretical constructs. It is necessary to summarize and analyze academic publications, educational and methodological works, regulatory documents, reference materials, and the practical application of military-technical translation/interpreting spanning the period of 1993–2026. Furthermore, it is essential to substantiate the theoretical and conceptual basis of military-technical translation/interpreting by delineating its object, subject matter, purpose, tasks, conceptual framework, and the specificity of its execution within the system of linguistic support for military forces. Other priority research tasks concerning military-technical translation/interpreting include: investigating the genre-stylistic specificity of military-technical texts; providing an academic description of various types of military-technical texts and developing their typology; systematizing the lexico-semantic and grammatical-syntactic difficulties inherent in military-technical translation/interpreting; determining the scope of the military-terminological (normative-codifying) activity of the military translator/interpreter; and refining the content and definitions of specialized terms, ultimately culminating in the compilation of an appropriate glossary.
